summary: Clarify split burst-pool fallback behavior and recurring soft 429s after org switchover
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightCart started a tenant/org switchover (subaccount migration) on 2026-03-09. After cutover we observe recurring 'soft' 429 responses for a subset of interactive chat and short-lived embedding requests. Errors present as 429 with Retry-After 1-3s and sporadic failures concentrated in short windows (30s-2m) roughly every 5–10 minutes.

Impact:
- ~4–8% of interactive chat messages and ~6% of small embedding batches receive 429s during the pattern window, causing user retries and visible errors in the customer UI.
- Affects production us-east BrightCart dedicated pool only.

Observed behavior:
- Pattern started immediately after BrightCart's subaccount routing change (org switchover) on 2026-03-09 22:00 UTC.
- 429s correlate with routing hits to a new burst pool backend and simultaneous health-check bursts from the migration coordinator.
- Logs show token-window depletion events and 'fallback to burst-pool' trace messages.

Expected behavior:
- During migration the platform should honor per-route/tenant burst credits and not produce repeated soft 429s when brief health-checks or ephemeral short-lived sessions occur. Fallback behavior should gracefully queue or route to compatible capacity without double-counting tokens.

Customer request:
- Clarify how split burst-pools and fallback routing count tokens during a tenant migration, and advise configuration or immediate mitigations the customer can apply to eliminate the recurring soft 429s.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) BrightCart performed subaccount switchover using 'tenant-migrate-v2' orchestrator at 2026-03-09 22:00 UTC.
2) Run normal interactive chat traffic to the same API key with concurrency ~30 connections and short messages (avg 12 tokens).
3) Simultaneously trigger periodic embedding micro-batches (10 items per batch) from a worker every 60s.
4) Observe ~4-8% 429s in HTTP responses during periodic 30s-2m windows and Retry-After values 1-3s.
5) Check routing logs for 'fallback=burst-pool' events and token-window depletion traces.

investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 09:15 - Liam O'Connor: Confirmed correlation between migration coordinator health-check spikes and token-window exhaustion in the dedicated pool's edge rate-limiter.

2026-03-10 10:02 - Priya Shah (SRE): Observed that when a route becomes 'split' between origin and new burst-pool, we emit consecutive refill checks causing duplicate accounting for very short-lived sessions (HTTP/2 multiplex and ephemeral keys).

2026-03-10 13:40 - Marco Rios (Serving): The fallback path increments tenant counters before origin confirms acceptance, so health-check fanout + short session warmups can consume burst credits faster than expected.
Hypothesis: Double-accounting during rapid route handover + health-check fanout is draining burst credits and producing soft 429s in periodic windows.
comments: 2026-03-10 08:55 - Sofia Mendes (Support): Hi BrightCart — we see the pattern and are investigating. Can you confirm if embedding workers were running scheduled warmups during the cutover?
2026-03-10 09:02 - BrightCart (Customer): Yes — we had background embedding workers configured to run every 60s; we can pause them if that helps.
2026-03-10 09:20 - Liam O'Connor (Eng): Thanks — please pause the embedding workers as a temporary mitigation. We're instrumenting rate-limiter traces now.

2026-03-10 12:05 - Priya Shah (SRE): Added an internal flag to suppress duplicate refill accounting for routes flagged as 'handover-pending' in the next canary. Need validation results before promoting widely.
2026-03-11 07:30 - BrightCart: Paused workers and saw immediate reduction in 429s. Customer requests explanation so they can safely resume workers with safe config.
2026-03-12 16:45 - Liam O'Connor: Proposing short-term config guidance and long-term fix. Posting recommended settings next.
recommended_mitigation: Short-term (immediate): Pause or stagger embedding worker schedules during a switchover and reduce concurrent short-lived sessions during route handover.
Short-term (platform): Apply temporary per-tenant burst-buffer increase for BrightCart (engineering change executed 2026-03-12 18:00 UTC).
Medium-term: Enable 'handover-pending' refill suppression flag in the dedicated pool for 3 releases to avoid duplicate accounting during migrations.
Long-term: Update fallback path to perform optimistic routing token checks only after origin ack; add rate-limiter instrumentation to detect near-simultaneous refill events.
resolution: 2026-03-12 18:00 - Applied temporary tenant burst-buffer increase; customer reported 90% reduction in 429s within 10 minutes.
2026-03-13 - Engineering created PR to suppress duplicate refill events during route handover: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rate-limiter/pull/3245
Planned rollout: Canary on 2026-03-20 with monitored metrics and roll-back plan. Owner: Priya Shah (SRE).
Follow-ups: Create runbook for customers performing tenant switchover recommending worker-stagger and contact path for temporary burst increases. Assigned to: Support Docs (Aisha Patel).
